healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system severely damaged by ongoing conflict since April 2023. Most hospitals in Khartoum and conflict zones are non-functional or operating at minimal capacity. Healthcare was already underfunded before the war.
qualityNotes: Healthcare infrastructure has been devastated by the ongoing civil conflict. Most hospitals in Khartoum are closed or damaged. Functioning facilities face severe shortages of staff, medications, and supplies. Port Sudan has become a hub for remaining healthcare services.
pharmacyHours: Irregular and unpredictable due to conflict. Some pharmacies in Port Sudan and unaffected areas operate 8am-6pm. Look for 'صيدلية' (Saydaliyya).
pharmacyTips: Medication supply chains are severely disrupted by the conflict. Counterfeit drugs are a significant concern. Bring all necessary medications from home in generous quantities.
prescriptionRules: No reliable prescription system currently functioning. Medications are sold based on availability. Quality and authenticity cannot be guaranteed.

restrictedMeds.name: Alcohol-based medications
restrictedMeds.note: Alcohol is prohibited under Sudanese law. Medications containing alcohol may be confiscated.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic substances
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly prohibited under Sudanese law. Severe penalties apply. Carry thorough documentation for any controlled medications.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English and Arabic listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring comprehensive supplies as local availability is extremely unreliable.

travelInsurance.tips: Most standard travel insurance policies exclude Sudan due to the active conflict. Specialist war-zone or humanitarian worker coverage is required. Medical evacuation coverage is absolutely essential. Verify your policy covers both medical and security evacuation.

required: Yellow fever (if arriving from endemic country)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required for travelers arriving from endemic areas. Malaria prophylaxis is essential — Sudan has year-round transmission. Cholera outbreaks occur, especially in conflict-affected areas. Consult a travel medicine specialist.

waterNotes: Tap water is unsafe throughout Sudan. The conflict has further damaged water infrastructure. Drink only bottled or purified water. Water purification equipment is essential.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked foods served hot. Avoid raw vegetables and unpeeled fruits. Food supply chains are disrupted. Cholera and typhoid are ongoing risks, especially in displacement camps.
medicalTourismNote: Sudan is not a medical tourism destination. Before the conflict, Sudanese traveled to Egypt, Jordan, or India for medical procedures.
metaDescription: Health guide for Sudan. Emergency info, conflict-impacted healthcare, vaccination needs, water safety, and medical evacuation guidance for travelers.

hospitals.name: Port Sudan Teaching Hospital
hospitals.notes: One of the few functioning major hospitals. Basic emergency and primary care. Some English-speaking staff. Port Sudan has become a critical healthcare hub during the conflict.

hospitals.name: Royal Care International Hospital
hospitals.notes: Private hospital that was among the best in Sudan pre-conflict. Current operational status is uncertain. Verify before relying on this facility.

hospitals.name: Sudan General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

pharmacyPhrases.phrase: عندي ألم في المعدة (Indi alam fil-ma'ida)

dentalCare.availability: Extremely limited due to ongoing conflict. Some private dental clinics may operate in Port Sudan.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care was limited before the conflict and is now virtually unavailable in most areas. Sterilization standards cannot be guaranteed.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, seek care in Port Sudan if accessible. Otherwise, evacuation to Egypt or Saudi Arabia is necessary.

mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy, UNHCR, or International SOS
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are virtually nonexistent during the conflict. Widespread trauma affects the population. International humanitarian organizations may offer limited support. Pre-arrange remote therapy options.

accessibilityInfo.overview: No accessibility infrastructure. Conflict damage has destroyed roads, bridges, and buildings across much of the country.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible transportation. Movement is restricted by conflict in many areas.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Sudan is not accessible for travelers with physical limitations under current conditions. Travel is strongly advised against by most governments.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity is critically impaired by the conflict. Any respiratory illness is difficult to treat.

insuranceClaimProcess: Cash payment required. Obtaining documentation may be extremely difficult during the conflict. Request any available receipts. File claims with your insurer after evacuation or departure.

commonCosts.note: Costs are low but healthcare quality is extremely poor. USD often preferred. Currency situation is volatile. Most humanitarian workers arrange care through their organizations.

medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Jeddah, Saudi Arabia or Nairobi, Kenya
medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for any serious condition. Port Sudan airport is the most reliable exit point during the conflict. Khartoum airport status is uncertain. Evacuation may be complicated by active fighting and airspace restrictions.

pharmacyChains.name: Hospital-attached pharmacies
pharmacyChains.where: Port Sudan and select functioning areas
